[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Core model: colored tokens lie on one or more cyclic conveyor belts. Large pixel arrows are controls: red shifts its belt one position in the left/counterclockwise direction; green shifts it right/clockwise. Colored four-corner brackets are fixed goal slots; all solid goal-colored tokens must occupy matching bracketed slots simultaneously. Belts may cross and share a cell. At a crossing, rotating either belt transfers the occupying token onto that belt. Targets do NOT lock: before rotating a crossing belt, park an already aligned token one step off the crossing on its other belt, then restore it afterward. Choose shortest circular routes and use crossings to route goal tokens. The x=0 green strip is the action budget; top horizontal bars show completed rounds. Round 1 was one 20-cell ring. Round 2 had an outer 26-cell rectangle plus two horizontal 10-cell belts and required parking.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Core model: movable tiles occupy cyclic belts; red controls shift a belt backward/counterclockwise and green controls shift it forward/clockwise (for vertical belts, green/up is backward and red/down forward). Some levels depict one global cycle as separated segments: round 4 had a 20-cell horizontal cycle ordered TL→TR→BL→BR, plus a similarly segmented vertical cycle, sharing four cross centers. Exact state-space/BFS over token positions and unit belt rotations yields minimum routes.
